name: Technical University of Denmark
about: DTU is a self-governing technical university founded in 1829, combining engineering and natural science with sustainability and work with industry. General Engineering is its current English undergraduate full degree, taught on the landscaped Lyngby campus north of Copenhagen. Ballerup is home to many of its Danish-taught BEng students.

programmes.name: General Engineering

sources.title: DTU – BSc in General Engineering
General Engineering is a three-year English BSc at Lyngby with four specialisations and design-build projects.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: All courses are English; about 60% of students are international. Year one combines maths, programming, physics, chemistry, biotechnology and design-build projects and introduces at least two specialisations. Choose by year two: Living Systems, Advanced Materials, Cyber Systems or Future Energy. Year three has optional exchange/company projects and a sixth-semester bachelor project. Most graduates continue to an MSc; each MSc has its own prerequisites.

programmes.description: The first year combines mathematics, programming, physics, chemistry and biotechnology and introduces at least two specialisations. Choose your direction by year two. The final year offers electives, exchange or a company project, followed by a sixth-semester bachelor project.

structure.teachingStyle: Lectures, student-directed learning and design-build group projects; teams grow from three towards ten members.
structure.placement: Company projects are optional and need company and DTU supervisors; this is not a guaranteed placement or compulsory BEng internship.
structure.studyAbroad: Semester 5 can be spent abroad, at DTU, at another Danish university or taking a partner online course.
structure.flexibility: Choose a specialisation by year two; the third year has electives and a final bachelor project.

programmes.about: An English engineering BSc at Lyngby: build a foundation in maths and science, work on design-build projects and choose from Living Systems, Advanced Materials, Cyber Systems and Future Energy.

sources.title: DTU accepts a 24-point IB Diploma with specific subject and English requirements.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: IB Diploma at least 24 points qualifies. Only retakes of an originally unpassed exam are accepted. Danish subjects: Mathematics A, English B, Physics B, Chemistry B. A qualifying IB Diploma plus passed English equivalent to Danish B/A exempts the language test. Otherwise IELTS Academic 6.5, Cambridge C1/C2 180, TOEFL iBT 88 or 4.5 for exams after 21 January (year unstated). Online-verifiable certificates only; IELTS/TOEFL remain verifiable on 5 July; no IELTS One Skill Retake; TOEFL recipient 1684.

requirements.label: Documented English proficiency
requirements.note: The English-test exemption requires a qualifying IB Diploma and a passed English subject equivalent to Danish English B or A; the separate English B subject requirement still applies. Course Results are not named for this exemption: confirm with DTU or supply an approved test. Otherwise IELTS Academic 6.5, Cambridge C1/C2 180 or TOEFL iBT 88 / 4.5 under the updated scale after 21 January (year unstated); check the current table. No IELTS One Skill Retake; online verification required. Where DTU grants conditional admission pending an English test, upload the passed result through UnistartDTU by 1 September (annual rule; confirm 2027).

sources.title: DTU current tariff is EUR15,000 annual tuition and EUR100 application fee for liable non-EU/EEA applicants.
sources.quote: Structured restatement: EU/EEA tuition state-covered. Most non-EU/EEA pay EUR100 by 15 March before processing; attach receipt. Successful applicants deduct it from first EUR7,500 semester payment (EUR7,400). Certain permanent/qualifying residence permits exempt fees, subject to evidence. Tuition EUR15,000 yearly or EUR7,500 per semester upfront; autumn due 1 August. No undergraduate scholarships/waivers. No 2027 tariff label.
